name: Olissippo Lapa Palace
insider_take: This 19th-century palace turned luxury hotel sits majestically in Lisbon's diplomatic quarter, where ambassadors and dignitaries have walked the same marble halls for over a century.
whats_special: Built in 1870 as a private palace, this Leading Hotels property features original azulejo tiles, crystal chandeliers, and palatial gardens with sweeping views over the Tagus River. The hotel's restaurant occupies a stunning winter garden conservatory, while the spa is housed in former palace stables.
pro_tip: Book a river-view room on the upper floors for breathtaking sunset vistas, and time your arrival for late afternoon when golden light illuminates the palace's neoclassical façade.
dont_miss: The hotel's private gardens are a hidden oasis in the city, perfect for morning coffee. The nearby Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga is just a 5-minute walk and houses Portugal's finest art collection, including the famous Panels of St. Vincent.
pros: Historic palace setting with elegant 19th-century architecture
Prime location in prestigious Lapa district near embassies
Stunning views over Tagus River and Lisbon cityscape
Leading Hotels of the World luxury standards and service
cons: Historic building may have traditional room layouts
